declared.title: Does Choice Mean Freedom and Well-Being?
declared.foundIn: recherche Crossref « does choice mean freedom and well-being » du 2026-11-22 (piste « choix et cultures non occidentales ») ; titre relevé sur Crossref : contrôle d'identité plus faible

population: review of research on choice in Western, non-Western and working-class samples; no Arab sample named in the abstract

findings.text: In non-Western cultures and among working-class Westerners, freedom and choice do not carry the meaning or weight they have for university-educated Westerners

support.sentence: However, this article reviews research that shows that in non-Western cultures and among working-class Westerners, freedom and choice do not have the meaning or importance they do for the university-educated people who have been the subjects of almost all research on this topic.

findings.text: Too much choice can bring a paralysing uncertainty, depression and selfishness (claim of a narrative review, no pooled data)

support.sentence: Too much choice can produce a paralyzing uncertainty, depression, and selfishness.

limits: narrative review: no pooled numbers, no protocol
the claim about too much choice is not tied to a measured effect in the abstract
allegiance: co-author B. Schwartz wrote « The Paradox of Choice », the idea under test here
